awards.label: Best Overall
awards.why: Zigbee 3.0 certified, pairs with an Echo's built-in hub or SmartThings, and handles up to 600 W of LED.

awards.label: Best Budget
awards.why: Under $20 and it replaces either or both switches in a 3-way. Works locally with Zigbee2MQTT.

awards.label: Best for No-Neutral Boxes

awards.label: Most Flexible

products.verdict: A standard Zigbee 3.0 switch from a major brand. It pairs with the Zigbee hub built into some Echo devices, so many people won't need to buy a hub at all.
pros: Zigbee 3.0 certified
Works with Echo devices that have a Zigbee hub, SmartThings, and other Zigbee 3.0 hubs
Rated for 600 W LED/CFL, 1,800 W incandescent, and 15 A ballast loads
Decora form factor with optional color change kits
cons: 3-way needs a Leviton DD0SR remote switch

products.model: Smart Light Switch (no neutral, single rocker)
products.verdict: The go-to switch for older boxes without a neutral, with the most reviews on this list. It's built around Aqara's hub and app.
pros: Installs without a neutral wire
528 reviews and 100+ bought in the past month
Works with Apple Home, Google, Alexa, and SmartThings through the Aqara hub
Cuts power if it overheats
cons: Needs an Aqara hub, sold separately
No-neutral switches don't route Zigbee traffic for other devices

products.verdict: Two independent switches in one gang, for a box where you want separate control of a light and a fan, or two lights.
pros: Controls two circuits from one gang
4.4-star rating, the highest here
Works with Apple Home, Google, and Alexa through the Aqara hub
Overheat protection

products.verdict: The neutral-wire version of Aqara's single switch. Pick it over the no-neutral model when you have a neutral, since it's a little cheaper.
pros: Cheaper than the no-neutral version
264 reviews
Apple Home, Google, and Alexa through the Aqara hub
Overheat protection

specs.hub: Aqara hub (Zigbee) or Thread border router (Matter)

products.verdict: Aqara's newer switch runs on Zigbee or Matter over Thread, wires with or without a neutral, and handles 3-way. The second button works as a wireless scene switch.
pros: Choose Zigbee or Matter over Thread
Works with or without a neutral wire
Single-pole and 3-way
Decoupled mode turns the buttons into wireless scene switches
Power monitoring and overload protection when a neutral is connected
cons: Power monitoring and overload protection need a neutral

pros: Under $20
Replace one or both switches in a 3-way
Local control with Home Assistant and Zigbee2MQTT
Screwless wallplate in the box
Indicator light can show status, location, or stay off
cons: Not for smart bulbs or dimming
Cloud features need the MOES hub

Tempered glass face

Works with Zigbee2MQTT
Remembers on/off state after a power cut
4.2-star rating
cons: 3-way means buying a second smart switch and linking them in the app
Needs a Tuya Zigbee hub for app and voice control

products.verdict: A neutral-optional wall switch that works with Home Assistant through Zigbee2MQTT. Reviews are mixed.
pros: Works with or without a neutral wire
Home Assistant support through Zigbee2MQTT
100+ bought in the past month
cons: App and voice control need a SONOFF Zigbee gateway

products.verdict: A no-neutral rocker that pairs with standard Zigbee 3.0 hubs such as SmartThings and Hubitat. Single-pole only.
pros: No neutral needed
Works with SmartThings, Hubitat, and other Zigbee 3.0 hubs
Supports LED loads down to 5 W
Matching dimmers and fan controls in the same style
cons: The power LED is only adjustable through the SmartLife hub

avoid.flag: "3way" in the title, no 3-way wiring in the listing, 1.5 A rating
avoid.verdict: The title promises a 3-way no-neutral Zigbee switch. The listing never explains how 3-way works, and its own spec table rates it at 1.5 A.
reasons: "3way" leads the title, but none of the bullets mention 3-way wiring or a companion switch.
The spec table lists a 1.5 A current rating, about 180 W at 120 V. Every other switch here is rated several times higher.
The bullets are generic ("multiple state settings") and don't name a single compatible hub.
For about the same price, the Martin Jerry and MOES switches above document their wiring and hub support.

systems_note: Brand-hub switches (Aqara, MOES, SONOFF) are shown with the systems their listings name.
